Safety Culture, Organizational Development and System Safety
Säkerhetskultur, organisationsutveckling och systemsäkerhet
paragraphs:
Valid for: 2026/27
Faculty: Faculty of Engineering LTH
Decided by: PLED C/D
Date of Decision: 2026-04-16

Depth of study relative to the degree requirements:  Second cycle, in-depth level of the course cannot be classified
      
      
Elective for: BME5, C4, R4-ss, RH4
Language of instruction: The course will be given in Swedish

The course is based on a system safety perspective that considers the interplay of man, technology, and organization (MTO). In relation to this, the aim of the course is to provide a knowledge base on the importance of an organization's safety culture for a safe, healthy and efficient organization or workplace. Through an organization's system safety work, risks are identified and reduced and objectives for safety are defined. The outcome of the system safety work and thus safety has a strong relationship with and is affected by the organization's safety culture, which are the shared values ​​and behaviours regarding risk and safety. The organizational safety culture can be challenged by new demands on production, technology and process development, changes in working methods and competence needs, as well as changes in safety attitudes and behaviours. The course provides students with the knowledge of change management and organizational development to achieve safe operations. The course provides knowledge about and develops the student’s understanding of the building blocks, challenges and opportunities of a safety culture, how the culture relates to safety, and shows methods for valuing and changing an organization's safety culture. The aim of the course is also to strengthen the student's ability to analyze and reflect—both individually and in groups—on factors that influence safety culture and organizational development. Furthermore, the student should be able to propose individual and organizational measures to enhance the safety culture.
The course relates to the UN's sustainable development goals through its overall focus on safety and risk and good conditions for people and the environment.

The course includes lectures, seminars, individual written assignments, group work, oral presentation and written exam. The course deals with different theoretical perspectives on system safety, safety culture and organizational development as well as the culture's relationship to safety outcome and risk behaviour. The safety culture is discussed as a driving force and as an outcome variable of organizational changes. Central aspects such as safety leadership, communication, risk perception and change management are treated. The safety culture’s relation to reporting of system weaknesses and learning for safety at the individual and organizational level and psychological safety are also touched upon. Methods and strategies for assessing and evaluating safety culture are included, as well as characteristics of various industries and organizations and their impact on risk / safety.

Grading scale: TH - (U, 3, 4, 5) - (Fail, Three, Four, Five)
Assessment:

The examination includes an individual written exam, written individual assignments, group work, oral presentation, attendance and active participation in discussion seminars. To pass the course, the student needs to be approved in all assessment parts.

The examiner, in consultation with Disability Support Services, may deviate from the regular form of examination in order to provide a permanently disabled student with a form of examination equivalent to that of a student without a disability.
